armLift.heroDesc1: An arm lift, medically known as brachioplasty, is a surgical procedure designed to remove excess skin and fat from the upper arms to create a firmer, more defined contour. It is most commonly sought by individuals who experience sagging or "bat wing" appearance of the arms after significant weight loss, ageing, or genetic skin laxity—changes that do not respond adequately to exercise alone.
armLift.heroDesc2: This procedure is intended for people who are close to their ideal weight but are left with loose, hanging skin along the inner or back portion of the upper arms. When performed correctly, an arm lift restores proportion to the arms, improves comfort in clothing, and enhances overall body balance.
armLift.heroDesc3: In Malaysia, arm lift surgery is classified as a regulated surgical procedure. It must be performed by a registered medical practitioner in a licensed healthcare facility, under standards regulated by the Ministry of Health Malaysia – Private Healthcare Services, which oversees surgical safety, facility licensing, and professional conduct.
armLift.mohMalaysia: The procedure is regulated by the Ministry of Health Malaysia
armLift.whatDesc: An arm lift (brachioplasty) is a surgical body contouring procedure that removes excess skin and fat from the upper arms—typically from the underarm area (axilla) to the elbow—to improve shape and reduce sagging. It is not a weight-loss treatment, but a contouring solution for skin that has lost its elasticity.
armLift.whatPoint1: The procedure removes excess loose skin
armLift.whatPoint2: The procedure improves arm contour and tone
armLift.causesDesc: As we age, our skin gradually loses collagen and elastin—the proteins responsible for firmness and elasticity. Combined with gravity, fluctuating weight, and reduced muscle tone, the upper arms can develop loose, hanging skin that may not respond to exercise alone.
armLift.typesDesc: Dr. Soma selects the specific technique based on your degree of skin laxity and desired outcome.
armLift.type1Desc: An incision runs from the armpit to the elbow along the inner arm. This allows for maximum excess skin removal and is ideal for significant skin laxity.
armLift.type1Feat1: This technique allows maximum skin removal
armLift.type2Desc: A shorter incision hidden in the armpit, suitable for patients with mild skin excess near the underarm only.
armLift.type2Feat1: This technique results in minimal scarring
armLift.type3Desc: For patients with excess skin that extends onto the side of the chest (lateral chest wall), often seen after massive weight loss.
armLift.benefitsDesc: An arm lift offers both functional and aesthetic improvements for patients struggling with excess upper arm skin.
armLift.benefit1Desc: Eliminates sagging 'bat wings' that don't respond to exercise.
armLift.benefit2Desc: Creates a more toned, defined upper arm contour.
armLift.benefit3Desc: Wear sleeveless clothing and move freely without self-consciousness.
armLift.benefit4Desc: Eliminates chafing or rashes caused by excess skin friction.
armLift.benefit5Desc: The improvement is permanent when weight remains stable
armLift.floatingBadgeDesc: Results are permanent as long as weight remains stable and healthy habits are maintained.
armLift.candidateSummary: Patients should have stable weight, significant skin laxity, good general health, and be non-smokers
armLift.compareNote: In some cases, arm lift and liposuction are combined for enhanced contouring.
armLift.recoveryDesc: Clear Timeline for Your Healing Journey
armLift.resPoint1c: Avoid raising arms above shoulder level
armLift.resPoint2a: Return to desk work or light duties
armLift.scarDesc: Scarring is an expected outcome of arm lift surgery. The incision is typically placed along the inner arm—where it is less visible—and extends from the armpit towards the elbow.
armLift.scarItem1Desc: Incisions are placed along the inner arm where they are less visible.
armLift.scarItem2Desc: Following aftercare instructions helps scars heal cleanly.
armLift.scarItem3Desc: Avoiding sun exposure prevents darkening of scars.
armLift.scarItem4Desc: Silicone sheets or gels can be used to support scar maturation.
armLift.scarNote: Most patients find that the improvement in arm contour outweighs the presence of scars — particularly as they fade over time.
armLift.scarFadeDesc: Initial scars may appear red or pink but typically fade significantly over 12–18 months, becoming flat and lighter in colour.
armLift.pricingDesc: The arm lift cost varies depending on several factors
armLift.priceFactor3: The procedure may be combined with liposuction
armLift.priceFactor4: The operating time affects the cost
armLift.faqDesc: Get answers to common concerns about arm lift surgery
armLift.faq1A: An arm lift is a surgical procedure that removes excess loose skin and, if needed, fat from the upper arms. It creates a more toned, contoured appearance, particularly for patients who have lost significant weight or developed skin laxity due to ageing.
armLift.faq2Q: Who is a good candidate for arm lift surgery?
armLift.faq2A: Ideal candidates include adults with sagging upper-arm skin that causes discomfort or self-consciousness, those at a stable weight, non-smokers (or willing to stop), individuals without medical conditions that impair healing, and people with realistic expectations about outcomes and scars.
armLift.faq3Q: What is the difference between an arm lift and liposuction?
armLift.faq3A: Liposuction removes excess fat but does not address loose skin. An arm lift removes redundant skin and tightens the remaining tissue. In some cases, both procedures are combined for optimal contouring.
armLift.faq4Q: How long does arm lift surgery take?
armLift.faq4A: Typically, the surgery takes 2–3 hours, depending on the extent of skin removal and whether liposuction is performed simultaneously.
armLift.faq5Q: What kind of anaesthesia is used?
armLift.faq5A: General anaesthesia is usually recommended. The specifics will be discussed during your consultation with Dr. Soma.
armLift.faq6Q: What is the expected recovery time?
armLift.faq6A: Most patients can return to desk-based work within 1–2 weeks. Strenuous activities, heavy lifting, and upper-body exercise are generally restricted for 4–6 weeks. Final contour becomes more visible at 3–6 months.
armLift.faq7A: Yes. Scars are a necessary part of the procedure. They typically run along the inner arm from the armpit towards the elbow. With proper care, scars fade significantly over time and can often be concealed.
armLift.faq8A: Yes — the removed skin will not return. However, maintaining a stable weight and following a healthy lifestyle is essential to preserve results.
armLift.faq9Q: Can an arm lift be combined with other procedures?
armLift.faq9A: Yes. Arm lifts can be combined with breast surgery, liposuction, tummy tucks, or other body contouring procedures as part of a comprehensive body reshaping plan.
armLift.faq10Q: Is arm lift surgery safe in Malaysia?
armLift.faq10A: When performed by a registered, board-certified plastic surgeon in a licensed healthcare facility — like Dr. Soma — arm lift surgery adheres to national medical standards. Dr. Soma operates under full monitoring protocols with a focus on patient safety.
armLift.safety1Desc: Arm lift surgery is a regulated procedure. Dr. Soma operates under national guidelines for private healthcare services.
armLift.safety2Desc: All procedures are performed in accredited, licensed medical facilities with full monitoring protocols.
armLift.safety3Desc: Dr. Soma is a registered medical practitioner and specialist plastic surgeon with years of experience in body contouring.
armLift.ctaDesc: Dr. Soma delivers personalised arm lift solutions with a focus on safety, natural contour, and long-lasting results.
